extracted.intended_audience: public company registrants (and their legal/compliance/advisory teams) preparing SEC climate-related disclosures
extracted.subtask_description: Final SEC rule text describing required climate-related disclosures for registrants (items such as transition plans, targets/goals, GHG metrics, offsets/RECs, management expertise, and related materiality/cross‑reference rules). Intended to guide drafting of Regulation S‑K / Regulation S‑X disclosure items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of climate-linked executive remuneration when material
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent a climate-related target or goal or other measure is a material element of a registrant's compensation of named executive officers, such information is required to be disclosed under Item 402(b) of Regulation S-K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a climate-related measure is a material component of named executive officers' pay, include the required Item 402(b) disclosure. Example/concern: commenters warned about potential costs and burdens for some companies if linking compensation disclosure to climate measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management relevant expertise disclosure (Instruction 2 to Item 1501)
rubrics_metrics.description: Relevant expertise of management in Item 1501(b)(1) may include, for example: prior work experience in climate-related matters; any relevant degrees or certifications; any knowledge, skills, or other background in climate-related matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete examples of management's climate-related expertise (experience, credentials, knowledge/skills/background) when disclosing governance and oversight of climate risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition plan disclosure as part of strategy (Item 1502)
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule includes transition plan disclosure as part of a registrant's disclosure about climate-related risks and their impact on the registrant's strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transition plan disclosure was moved to 17 CFR 229.1502; registrants should disclose transition plans in strategy discussion (see also cross-references to prior proposed location and the Proposing Release).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of offsets and RECs used for targets/goals
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules require disclosure of used carbon offsets or RECs only as part of the targets and goals disclosure requirements (and the final rules also require certain disclosures of offsets and RECs under the Regulation S-X amendments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants may elect to provide target/goal disclosure as part of strategy or transition plan disclosure; to streamline Subpart 1500, offsets/RECs disclosure is required only in targets/goals section. See 17 CFR 210.14-02(e)(1) for Reg S‑X linkages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of carbon offsets
rubrics_metrics.description: Carbon offsets represent an emissions reduction or removal of greenhouse gases in a manner calculated and traced for the purpose of offsetting an entity's GHG emissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule added 'avoidance' to the definition (offset can represent avoidance, reduction, or removal). Examples: protecting a forest (avoidance), switching to wind/solar (reduction), carbon capture and storage (removal). Cite Proposing Release, section II.C.2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Renewable Energy Certificate (REC)
rubrics_metrics.description: An REC, consistent with EPA's commonly used definition, means a credit or certificate representing each purchased megawatt-hour (1 MWh or 1000 kilowatt-hours) of renewable electricity generated and delivered to a registrant's power grid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish RECs from offsets: RECs address Scope 2 (purchased electricity) whereas offsets address Scope 1–3. See Proposing Release, section II.I.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish offsets vs RECs and disclose scope addressed
rubrics_metrics.description: Offsets are used to address a company's GHG emissions (Scopes 1, 2, and 3) by verifying external project reductions; RECs are used solely to address indirect GHG emissions associated with purchased electricity (Scope 2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When disclosing use of offsets/RECs, clarify which Scope(s) each instrument is intended to address so investors can assess relevance to registrant's emissions profile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose nature and source of offsets/RECs
rubrics_metrics.description: The nature of an offset refers to whether it represents carbon avoidance, reduction, or removal. The nature of an REC refers primarily to whether it is bundled or unbundled. The source of an offset or REC refers to the party that has issued the offset or REC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters recommended disclosure of such details so investors can evaluate effectiveness of a registrant's transition strategy. Final rule references 17 CFR 229.1504(d) for required detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify and disclose bundled vs unbundled RECs
rubrics_metrics.description: A bundled REC is one that is sold together with the generated electricity directly to the consumer or reseller whereas an unbundled REC is one that has been separated from and sold without delivery of the generated electricity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unbundled RECs are counted, some commenters (e.g., CalPERS) suggested registrants disclose totals with and without use of unbundled RECs for each emissions scope. Note differences between compliance and voluntary REC markets and certification status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose REC market type and certification status
rubrics_metrics.description: Utilities may purchase RECs in a compliance market to comply with a state's renewable portfolio standard whereas a non-utility company may purchase RECs in a voluntary market. RECs purchased in a compliance market must meet certain standards and must be certified by an approved certifying group; voluntary market RECs may or may not be certified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose whether RECs were purchased in compliance vs voluntary markets and whether they were certified, to inform investor assessment of quality and reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include 'avoidance' in offset classification
rubrics_metrics.description: At the recommendation of commenters, the Commission added 'avoidance' to the definition of carbon offset (in addition to reduction and removal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide examples and classify offsets accordingly (e.g., protecting a forest = avoidance). See Ceres and other commenter resources for evaluating credits.

rubrics_metrics.name: GHG gases included in the definition
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed definition of 'greenhouse gases' included: carbon dioxide (CO2); methane (CH4); nitrous oxide (N2O); nitrogen trifluoride (NF3); hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs); perfluorocarbons (PFCs); and sulfur hexafluoride (SF6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This list aligns with gases commonly referenced by international and regulatory authorities (Kyoto Protocol, EPA, GHG Protocol). Registrants should use these constituent gases when reporting GHGs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct vs indirect emissions definitions (scopes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct emissions are GHG emissions from sources that are owned or controlled by a registrant, whereas indirect emissions are GHG emissions that result from the activities of the registrant but occur at sources not owned or controlled by the registrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the GHG Protocol corporate accounting definitions to classify emissions (scope 1 = direct, scope 2 = indirect from purchased electricity, scope 3 = other indirect upstream/downstream).

rubrics_metrics.name: Upstream and downstream Scope 3 examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Upstream emissions include emissions attributable to goods and services that the registrant acquires, transportation of goods to the registrant, and employee business travel and commuting. Downstream emissions include use of the registrant's products, transportation of products to customers, end-of-life treatment of sold products, and investments made by the registrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting Scope 3, identify which upstream/downstream categories are included and provide examples relevant to the registrant's operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: GHG intensity reporting (proposed) — units specification
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rules would have required the disclosure of GHG intensity to be in terms of metric tons of CO2e per unit of total revenue and per unit of production for the fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule discussion notes elimination of some proposed intensity requirements; where intensity is used, specify units (CO2e per revenue unit and per production unit) and be consistent year‑to‑year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of progress toward targets and linkage to financials
rubrics_metrics.description: When disclosing its targets or goals, a registrant should disclose any data that indicate whether the registrant is making progress toward meeting the target and how such progress has been achieved, including how progress toward targets or goals links to the financial statements because capital expenditures made in implementing transition plans are a key metric for investors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide quantitative progress metrics, describe actions taken, and explain financial impacts (capex) and linkages to reported financials where material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of disclosure for voluntary/internal targets
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters recommended clarifying that disclosure of voluntary targets or goals applies only to targets and goals that have been publicly announced by the registrant, its subsidiaries that are separate registrants, or its significant subsidiaries; internal targets may be less developed and not required to be disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants should consider limiting required disclosure of voluntary targets to those publicly announced to avoid forcing disclosure of internal, undeveloped targets; note commenter recommendations (PwC, Amazon).

rubrics_metrics.name: Update obligations tied to materiality (no update if target not required)
rubrics_metrics.description: No update about targets and goals would be required to be disclosed if the underlying targets or goals are not required to be disclosed (e.g., because the target or goal is no longer material).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain materiality assessment: only update disclosures for targets/goals that remain material and required; otherwise, updates are not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid redundancy — disclose material expenditures in most appropriate item and cross-reference
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent that there is any overlapping disclosure of material expenditures in response to multiple Items (e.g., transition plan, strategy, activities to mitigate/adapt), to avoid redundancy, a registrant should provide disclosure of material expenditures regarding the Item where, in its assessment, such disclosure is most appropriate, and then cross-reference to this disclosure when responding to the other Items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cross-referencing across Subpart 1500 items to avoid duplicated material expenditures disclosure; choose the Item that best fits and cross‑reference elsewhere.
